content:
What do people think about introducing the abbrev Nonneg R in place of {x : R // 0 ≤ x}. The latter is ubiquitous throughout mathlib but has the tendency to be used inconsistently and does not print well. I made a PR: #41134.

@Snir Broshi pointed me to the previous discussion here: general > backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency @ 💬

(Maybe same with Pos R?)

Martin Winter said:

(Maybe same with Pos R?)

Also mentioned at #mathlib4 > reducible constructors for PNat @ 💬 btw

i think making it an abbrev for a subtype is probably not good enough from a transparency point of view, since i suspect we might want to add some instances specific to this case (and also, lean may become confused about the resulting type of constructors, particularly since one can rewrite the fun x => 0 ≤ x argument)... i'd personally recommend a two-field structure instead, making it entirely separate from Subtype.

It seems the abbrev change in the PR went through without any trouble. But I have no deeper understanding of these things so I have no opinion here. I just thought I try this proactively. Regarding the structure I will leave this to someone else. But you have my PR to fall back to now. Snir mentioned in a comment on my PR that it could be a reasonable intermediate step towards the structure.

I'll include the comment here: We could either

  • first introduce it as a seamless abbrev like you're doing here and later fight with making it a structure, or
  • introduce it as a structure without using it anywhere and later migrate material.

I'm not sure which is best, but my instinct is that the second option is because it let's us migrate incrementally.

Have there been any attempts at creating the structure version of Nonneg since June? If not, could we reconsider the abbrev version of #41134 as an intermediate solution? The PR compiles fine without any problems.
